In addition, GGWB competes in DMV competitions, such as Re;Konnect 2023, with a select competitive team. We tend to hold events on Tuesdays and Fridays from 6-8pm, which include workshops, showcases, game nights, and more! No experience necessary, all levels welcome! You can find out more info about our socials and join our Discord server through this link! https://linktr.ee/umd.ggwb

name: Gift of Life at the University of Maryland
description: The Gift of Life Campus Ambassador Program raises awareness for the bone marrow donation process. In collaboration with the Gift of Life, one of the nation’s public bone marrow and blood stem cell registries, the Campus Ambassador Program (CAP) organizes events, campaigns, trainings, and seminars to register new potential donors, raise monetary funds, and educate the community about the bone marrow donation process. CAP is dedicated to expanding the bone marrow registry and supporting those who have been affected by cancer.

name: Girls Into VC at UMD
description: The Girls into VC at UMD Club exists to empower and prepare female students to enter and excel in venture capital and entrepreneurship. We are committed to breaking down barriers in the investment world by providing education, mentorship, networking opportunities, and hands-on experience in evaluating startups and understanding the venture capital ecosystem.

name: Girls Who Lead - University of Maryland Chapter
description: GWL focuses on training young women in all things policy, business, law, entrepreneurship, and advocacy. We aim to increase the number of women in leadership, building the next generation to create real change for communities across the US and globally.

name: Global Communities Student Association
description: The Global Communities Student Association (referred to as “the GCSA” throughout the rest of this document) is the student-run organization within the Honors Global Challenges & Solutions (HGLO) program that promotes cultural values as well as understanding different cultures and cooperation between cultures through community building, academic activities, and events. GCSA does not restrict membership or discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, age, national origin, political affiliation, physical or mental disability, religion, protected veteran status, genetic information, personal appearance, or on the basis of rights secured by the First Amendment of the United States Constitution. GCSA does not charge students membership fees. Students who want to be active members of GCSA do not have to pay membership dues. Dues are not required for voting or active membership.

name: Global Dental Brigades at the University of Maryland, College Park
description: Global Dental Brigades is the world’s largest student-led global health and sustainable development organization. We empower under-resourced communities around the world to facilitate the implementation of sustainable healthcare solutions while fostering local cultures. We plan annual service trips to less developed countries in order to assist local dentists in providing urgent preventative dental care and conduct educational dental hygiene workshops in communities with limited access to healthcare. In doing so, our volunteers are given the opportunity to shadow licensed dentists in a fast-paced, hands-on manner unique to this experience.

name: Global Health Leaders
description: Global Health Leaders at the University of Maryland brings together pre-medical and pre-health students, as well as professionals, who are devoted to enhancing global healthcare. Our mission, as members of Global Health Leaders, is to promote engagement in global healthcare through events and activities, thereby contributing to overall advancement in healthcare worldwide.

name: Global Terps for a Greener Future Collective
description: The Global Terps for a Greener Future Collective (GTFGC) is a student-led organization at the University of Maryland dedicated to advancing sustainability through global collaboration and education. Supported by the UMD Sustainability Fund, GTFGC connects students to address pressing environmental challenges from a multidisciplinary and intercultural perspective. Members participate in workshops, projects, and research that promote sustainable practices in international education while developing leadership skills and a global outlook. By fostering dialogue and innovation, the Collective strives to build a more sustainable campus community and a healthier planet for future generations.

name: Google Developer Student Club
description: The Google Developer Student Club at UMD is a community that provides an educational and creative environment for undergraduate students interested in various technologies and programming languages. To join, register an account on our official chapter website and join the discord! Chapter site: https://gdg.community.dev/gdg-on-campus-university-of-maryland-college-park-united-states/ Discord: https://discord.gg/rYYu6sWK9P

name: GraceLife Bible Church
description: The name of our student group is GraceLife Bible Church (GBC) at the University of Maryland. This student group is a student chapter recognized by GraceLife Bible Church, a Maryland Church with its primary location in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Our purpose is to build a community of people who are transformed by Jesus Christ. We seek to create meaningful relationships among our members, creating a strong community rooted in faith and fellowship. Through discipleship, outreach, and intentional engagement, we aim to expand and reach the UMD student body with the love and truth of Jesus Christ.

name: Graduate Art History Association
description: The Graduate Art History Association (GAHA) is a student organization created by the graduate students of the Art History & Archaeology Department. GAHA fosters a collegial environment among graduate students and provides exciting opportunities for professional development. In general, GAHA exists as a forum for students of the department to get together and discuss any issues that may pertain to their work in the department, including professional development opportunities/strategies, requirements for degree fulfillment, and anything else that students bring to the table, as well as providing opportunities to actively engage in the DC local art scene and the broader scholarly community.

name: Graduate Association for Technology and Environmental Science
description: GATES is established for the expressed purpose of creating a unified, supportive community for Graduate Students advised by Environmental Science and Technology (ENST) Faculty to discuss and explore improvements to the graduate student experience; organize academic, professional, and social activities; and foster relationships between GATES members. This organization is also intended to facilitate communication between GATES members and ENST Faculty and Staff.

name: Graduate Creative Writers’ Association
description: GCWA is founded to facilitate communication between English MFA students and the English department at the University of Maryland as well as develop leadership skills as instructors and writers. The organization fosters a community for writers to share resources and opportunities (e.g. publishing, fellowships) inside and outside of the university. The organization is also in partnership with the graduate literary journal Brack Water Magazine with the aim to cultivate a broader literary presence.

name: Graduate Science Policy at UMD
description: SPG is established for the expressed purpose of advocating for the inclusion of science in all levels of decision-making. The primary goal of this organization is to assist its members, other graduate students, and graduate student organizations in the engagement of society with science, particularly around applications of science within decision-making contexts.

name: Graduate Student Government
description: Graduate Student Government (GSG) is the official representative body for graduate students at the University of Maryland, College Park. It is comprised of the executive (E-board) and legislative (Assembly) branches. We meet monthly at our General Assembly Meetings, which are open to all graduate students. GSG is funded by the Graduate Student Activities Fee. Preamble We, the graduate students of the University of Maryland, College Park, in order to secure and protect the welfare, rights, and interests of all graduate students at this institution, do hereby ordain and establish this Constitution of the graduate student body, and, in so doing, outline a graduate student body organization charged with serving and representing all graduate students under a unified organization. Article 1: Name and Purpose 1.1. Name 1.1.A. The name of this organization shall be the Graduate Student Government of the University of Maryland, College Park (GSG). 1.2. Purpose 1.2.A. It shall be the supreme graduate student governmental body for implementing the objectives set forth in the Preamble, subject only to the laws of our state and the nation, and the right of review by the President of the University of Maryland, College Park, or his/her specifically designated representative. 1.2.B. It shall formulate policies promoting and governing the activities and welfare of graduate students of the University of Maryland, College Park, and it shall advise the Associate Provost for Academic Affairs and Dean of the Graduate School, Senior Vice President for Student Affairs and Provost, the Graduate Council, the University Senate, the President of the University, the Maryland General Assembly, and any other relevant agency or organization on the graduate student viewpoint concerning all matters affecting graduate students. 1.2.C. It shall be responsible for the allocation of the Student Activity Fee of graduate students and supervise and provide input regarding all other Mandatory Fees. 1.2.D. It shall act to improve the quality of education and enhance the quality of life of all graduate students. Contact Info: Website: www.gsg.umd.edu Email: gsg-office@umd.edu Facebook: @gsg.umd Twitter: @GSGUMD

name: Graduate Students with Disabilities
description: PROFILE PICTURE HISTORY: The "UMD accessibility terp" was created by Samuel diBella in 2023 to represent the UMD disability community, which includes graduate students, undergrads, faculty, staff, and neighbors. We distribute stickers and pins with this logo to raise awareness of UMD accessibility resources and foster connection and support among those with disabled identities. PROFILE PICTURE ALT TEXT: The "UMD accessibility terp" is inspired by and features the colors of the disability pride flag, created by Ann Magill in 2021. It features a green and yellow turtle on a black background, holding a heart with red, gold, white, blue, and green stripes. The parallel lines represent interdependence and cross-disability solidarity. Red represents physical disabilities, gold is cognitive and intellectual disabilities, white is nonvisible and undiagnosed disabilities, blue is psychiatric disabilities, and green is sensory disabilities. The black background mourns disabled people who have died due to negligence, suicide, rebellion, illness, and eugenics. (Source: RespectAbility.) The "terp" is also encircled by the URL for the UMD accessibility website, accessibility.umd.edu. GWD BRIEF HISTORY: We formed in early 2023 when our founder returned from a leave of absence and reached out to ADS to connect with other grad assistants. We changed our name from UMD Grad Assistants with Disabilities to UMD GWD (Graduate S tudents with disabilities ) since we realized there was nowhere for graduate students without assistantships to join. This group is intended to be a private, confidential, accessible, and safe space for graduate students to chat and get to know each other, without ableist norms or expectations. regularly collaborate with other student orgs like QWD and DICE, as well as the Disability Cultural Center, and the Student Affairs affinity group for disabled employees, and occasionally collaborate with individuals at other MD/USM institutions. To join our Whatsapp conversations, please reach out to our president and/or advisor. You can also find resources here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OJhwPMLKpAJx5qmtc8apeMCpkqYn8e00EfFtCIQlTQ4/edit and some of our advocacy priorities here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1tu8TNiwEnbgKAnlnxjYEbBXL39cg225WxkKdLNVMYqU/edit

name: Graduate Students' Association of Ghana - UMD
description: This is organization for Ghanaian graduate students at the University of Maryland.

name: Greek Basketball Association at the University of Maryland
description: The Greek Basketball Association (GBA) at the University of Maryland provides a structured and competitive basketball league exclusively for fraternity members during the fall semester. Focused on fostering sportsmanship, teamwork, and leadership, the GBA organizes weekly league play throughout September and October, with each team guaranteed 10 regular-season games. The season culminates in an exciting on-campus, single-elimination playoff tournament to crown the GBA champion.

name: Greek Heritage Society
description: A close-knit group of students, who strive to keep Greek culture alive at the University of Maryland, College Park and make lifelong friendships! We strive to sustain and expand Hellenic culture on campus through our cultural and religious events.

name: Green Roots
description: Green Roots exists to advance sustainable and urban agriculture through innovative techniques. We grow food through hydroponics, which is the production of plants without soil, by integrating a number of diverse disciplines. Recently, we began to construct and maintain aquaponic systems to produce fish and produce without fertilizer inputs. Green Roots is devoted to research, education, and community service. We explore issues related to hydroponics/aquaponics, design hydroponic/aquaponic systems, educate the public, and are working toward marketing our produce to students through a Community Supported Agriculture (CSA) model. Join our GroupMe!

name: Grey Matters UMD
description: Grey Matters UMD is dedicated to advancing public understanding of neuroscience, fostering active engagement within the scientific community, and cultivating proficient science communicators through collaborative publications. We envision Grey Matters as more than just a journal; it is a vibrant and inclusive community where students are empowered to delve into the depths of scientific literature, articulate their discoveries with clarity and precision, and cultivate essential interpersonal skills through teamwork and collaboration. At Grey Matters, we recognize the multidimensional nature of scientific inquiry and its intersection with various disciplines. Our mission extends beyond traditional boundaries, encompassing not only the realms of neuroscience but also embracing diverse fields such as art, design, English, and philosophy. By integrating these diverse perspectives, we create a dynamic platform where creativity and analytical rigor converge. Through our publications, Grey Matters expands on conventional academic journals by offering a rich tapestry of scientific exploration intertwined with artistic expression and literary craftsmanship. Each issue represents a synthesis of knowledge, blending empirical evidence with imaginative interpretations of complex concepts in neuroscience. Our approach not only educates but also inspires, igniting curiosity and fostering a deeper appreciation for the wonders of the brain.

name: Gymkana Troupe
description: Gymkana is an outreach organization that provides an opportunity for University students to participate in gymnastic and acrobatic activities and, through them, inspire healthy choices.

name: H2OPE at the UMDCP
description: Bridge H2OPE is a nonprofit organization based in the state of Maryland and founded in 2018 at Trinity College (originally H2OPE TC) with a mission to help raise awareness and fund efforts to provide access to clean drinking water in rural communities in Ethiopia. The organization works to support sustainable water solutions through fundraising, awareness-building, and community-driven initiatives. As a parent organization, Bridge H2OPE oversees and supports its growing network of collegiate chapters nationwide, empowering students to engage in global health advocacy and service. The University of Maryland, College Park chapter will continue this mission by mobilizing students to raise awareness, fund clean water projects, and contribute to meaningful, long-term impact in underserved communities.

name: Habesha's In Tech
description: The mission of Habeshas In Tech is to provide students in the tech industry with a community that is both encouraging and cooperative. The club helps its members grow professionally and personally by offering mentorship, networking opportunities, and professional development activities. It also gives members access to industry experts' advice and experiences.

name: Habitat for Humanity
description: To fund and build simple, decent affordable housing for low-income families. To involve individual students as well as student organizations and classes in working toward this common goal. To educate the University of Maryland community about the importance of eliminating barriers to adequate and affordable housing.

name: Hack4Impact-UMD
description: Note: We do not approve unsolicited join requests. If you're interested in joining, feel free to complete our interest form . Hack4Impact-UMD is a chapter of the national Hack4Impact organization, a 501(c)3 nonprofit with chapters in the US and Canada. The group is dedicated to creating software for social good. As part of this group, you can take up a role as a product designer, software developer, and/or product manager for our various software projects. You'll also be able to immerse yourself in the many professional development workshops, mentorship, and recruitment events we host with our corporate partners.

name: Health Equity Alliance
description: HEAL (Health Equity Alliance) is a multidisciplinary student organization dedicated to advancing health equity and empowering students from all academic backgrounds to make meaningful social impact. We focus on addressing health disparities through education, advocacy, community engagement, interdisciplinary collaboration, and innovative problem-solving. Our mission is to create a space where students interested in public health, medicine, policy, law, business, research, global health, and community service can work together to address modern health challenges. HEAL hosts workshops, policy discussions, advocacy events, and hands-on service initiatives that promote health literacy, equity, and access. We welcome students of all majors and levels of experience, and we strive to build a diverse, supportive, and collaborative community committed to improving health outcomes locally and globally.

name: Health Policy and Management Student Association
description: The Health Policy and Management Student Organization (HPMSA) is an organization for students in the HLSA Department of the UMD School of Public Health. The mission of HPMSA is to foster networking opportunities and strengthen MHA and MPH students’ personal and professional skills. All graduate students enrolled in the Master of Health Administration degree program, Master of Public Health degree in the Health Equity program, and Master of Public Health degree in the Health Policy Analysis & Evaluation program at the University of Maryland, College Park are eligible for membership. Members join committees aligned with their interests and are encouraged to partake in campus activities, community outreach, social events, mentoring, and other networking opportunities. If interested in joining or creating a partnership, please email us today! hmpsaumd@gmail.com

name: Health-Link Society
description: We are a service-oriented organization committed to fostering unity and mentorship among the next generation of pre-health students, all within the spirit of volunteerism.

name: Hearing and Speech Sciences Graduate Student Association
description: The Hearing and Speech Sciences Graduate Student Association is an organization led by students dedicated to supporting and connecting graduate students in Hearing and Speech Sciences. Our goal is to foster a collaborative and supportive graduate student community through academic, professional development, and community-building activities. Activities may include regular writing and study sessions, peer support, professional development opportunities, social events, and other programs that promote graduate student engagement and success.

name: Hearts for the Homeless College Park
description: Email h4h.umd@gmail.com for any questions you might have! Follow our Instagram page: https://www.instagram.com/h4h.umd/

name: Hearts In Action
description: Hearts in Action is an organization committed to making a lasting, positive impact in the College Park community. We address the needs of financially underserved individuals and families through year-round initiatives, including clothing and food drives, holiday gift programs, and educational supply distributions. By partnering with local homeless shelters and organizing community outreach events, we strive to ensure the well-being of all people—regardless of age, gender, or background. Our mission extends beyond material support: we aim to foster a culture of care, kindness, and social responsibility. Through hands-on involvement, students gain valuable leadership experience while building a more inclusive and compassionate campus and community.

name: Help Center
description: The Help Center (301-314-4357 or HELP), a student-led peer-to-peer counseling and crisis intervention service, was established over 50 years ago to provide a unique student support and mental health service for the campus community. Our team of trained peer counselors provides free and confidential telephone and drop-in peer counseling and referrals. Calls can range from concerns about academic issues to sexual assault; no issue is too big or too small. We also provide pregnancy tests and sexual health supplies, without charge, through our drop-in service. The Help Center is located in Room 3105 on the 3rd floor of the South Campus Dining Hall. Hours of Operation: Monday & Tuesday: 4:00 p.m. - 12:00 a.m. Wednesday: 8:00 p.m. - 12:00 a.m. Thursday & Friday: 4:00 p.m - 8:00 p.m. Drop-In Services are available Monday, Tuesday, & Thursday, 4:00 – 7:00 p.m. Notes: Hours are subject to counselor availability during the summer and winter breaks. Drop-in services are subject to change.

name: Helping Hand at UMD
description: We are a chapter of Helping Hand for Relief and Development, a global humanitarian relief organization that responds to human sufferings in emergency and disaster situations around the world. HHRD at UMD provides volunteer opportunities and educational events to raise awareness and contribute to humanitarian issues and causes both locally and internationally. We strive to build a strong community of passionate and dedicated volunteers who give back to the community.

name: Her Voice Matters
description: An organization dedicated to give women of color a safe space to talk about difficult topics.

name: Hermandad de Sigma Iota Alpha, Inc
description: As Hermanas of Hermandad de Sigma Iota Alpha Inc., our mission is to uphold the goals set forth by our thirteen founding mothers. We pledge to formalize, cultivate, and foster bonds amongst each other as sisters and abide by respect, trust, communication, professionalism, and accountability. Our goals are: To constantly strive towards the expansion of awareness of the Latino and diverse cultures. To promote sisterhood and leadership among our members. To serve as models of excellence in education and achievement among women. We fulfill our mission and uphold our goals through educational programming, community service, and personal development.

name: Hindu Student Council
description: We aim to increase campus awareness of the Hindu religion and culture. We plan several events each semester of both religious and cultural nature.

name: History Graduate Student Association
description: The University of Maryland HGSA exists to foster an intellectual community and share ideas and experiences. The HGSA promotes intellectual exchange both at formal history department events and in informal gatherings of fellow graduate students though parties, meetings, happy hours, and a lively e-mail list serv. The HGSA also serves as an advocate for graduate students in issues of administration and faculty decision-making concerning prospective changes to the graduate program. Our most important role is to serve as representatives in the formulation of new graduate policies and to allow the voice and experiences of graduate students to be heard in faculty meetings. All History graduate students are members and are invited to all events. In addition to hosting this web site, the HGSA promotes a Graduate Teaching Colloquium Series, a series designed for and by graduate students to develop as educators. The HGSA is affiliated with the Graduate Student Government, which serves all UM graduate students. General meetings are held on a regular basis on the 3rd floor of Francis Scott Key Hall. All members are encouraged to attend.

name: History Undergraduate Association
description: The History Undergraduate Association (HUA) connects undergraduates that share an interest in history. We typically host two events a month, including social hours, historical discussions with professors, trivia nights, and more!

name: Hong Kong Student Association
description: The Hong Kong Student Association (HKSA) is dedicated to promoting awareness and appreciation of Hong Kong’s identity—its food, traditions, language, and culture. We provide a welcoming space for students of Hong Kong heritage or anyone interested in learning more about Hong Kong. Through social events, cultural celebrations, and collaborations with other student groups, HKSA aims to build community, foster understanding, and celebrate a home away from home!

name: Horticulture Club
description: The Horticulture Club is a social club whose purpose is to foster a relationship between plants and people within and around the University of Maryland, through excursions, workshops, and community engagement. We welcome all members of our community to join our club. No level of horticultural experience or knowledge is required. Come grow with us!

name: HOSA Future Health Professions Chapter at the University of Maryland
description: HOSA Future Health Professions is a medical competition organization. There are so many competitive, recognition, and team events to participate in at the state and international level. Anyone wanting to further their medical career is encouraged to join. And every year, HOSA holds the international leadership conference where chapters across the globe come together to compete.

name: House of Prayer
description: Founded on the scripture 1 Kings 9:3 NKJV: " And the Lord said to him: “I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you have made before Me; I have consecrated this house which you have built to put My name there forever, and My eyes and My heart will be there perpetually.” We hope that through this ministry, many students will become fervent in the place of prayer, and even lead students who don’t know Christ to develop a personal relationship with Him as well. House of Prayer was founded because the founding members saw that there is a need to emphasize to believers and new believers the importance of prayer and how to pray effectively. We want to build strong foundations in our faith, cultivate a place of fellowship, and build a community where people feel safe to express their deepest troubles, stressors, and anxieties. Through this ministry, many will come to find solace in the presence of God, ultimately building spiritually mature habits that can be implemented within their day-to-day lives.

name: Human Development Student Association
description: The Human Development Student Association is a student organization for those interested in Human Development. This organization will provide students with career development resources and internship opportunities while also fostering a sense of community within the HD department.

name: Humanities Society
description: The Humanities Society is established to enrich the collegiate experience through participation in arts and humanities related activities, while fostering a sense of community throughout the University of Maryland and surrounding areas.

name: Humanity First @ UMD
description: - PLEASE COMPLETE THIS FORM to join and acquire contact information for any upcoming events - > Membership Form The primary objective of the Humanity First Student Organization at UMD is to advocate for human life by means of undertaking disaster relief efforts, as well as to alleviate suffering and promote human development for socially disadvantaged communities in partnership with Humanity First USA—the organization’s subsidiary. Additional objectives include putting our members' efforts to helping the local community of UMD while upholding the missions and values of Humanity First USA to better assist our members in serving our community locally and globally.

name: Hunger Free Zone
description: Our mother organization - Hunger Free Zone (HFZ) - took on a goal to share and care for the impoverished people in Maryland. On our free vegan food truck we have been: - feeding the homeless, targeting spots where people congregated that were struggling - and then to recovery houses (people suffering from substance abuse or personal difficulties of life) - apartment buildings for the people who make less than $30,000 a year and also - senior citizen homes. We go out 6 days a week with the determination to share a hot healthy vegan meal and show the people we care. The smiles and joyful thanks and blessings from these people give proof that we are making a difference. The happiness and psychological comfort of a food truck dedicated to them gives the hope for a better day. We UMD students are increasing our impact on sharing and caring. We put the freshly prepared delicious food in food warmer containers and load it on our gourmet food truck. Then take it to our dedicated sites and distribute it. HFZ prepares fresh, delicious, highly nutritious, and world class culinary vegan meals to the most needy in Maryland. HFZ is taking the first step in solving long term problems of hunger in the community. We have bought HFZ to the UMD community to bring awareness and spread this message of love amongst our student and staff community once a week! As HFZ visits other college campuses, we hope more students visit us weekly for a free vegan feast and wonderful association!

name: IEEE @ UMD
description: We empower students interested in ECE to achieve more as they journey through UMD. We do this by hosting professional, social, and academic events. We are associated with IEEE, but there is no membership fee required to be in our club.

name: IEEE EPS
description: The IEEE Electronics Packaging Society is the leading international forum for scientists and engineers engaged in the research, design and development of revolutionary advances in microsystems packaging and manufacturing. Its objectives are scientific, literary, and educational in character. The Society strives for the advancement of the theory and practice of electrical and electronics engineering and of the allied arts and sciences, and the maintenance of a high professional standing among its members and others and with special attention of such aims within the field of interest of the Society. The EPS promotes close cooperation and exchange of technical information among its members and others through technical conferences and workshops, peer-reviewed publications, and collaboration with other organizations. It is one of 38 technical Societies within the IEEE.

name: iGEM at the University of Maryland
description: The purpose of the University of Maryland iGEM team is to provide undergraduate students interested in the sciences a means to compete in the annual International Genetically Engineered Machine competition. Students will be part of a team with other students interested in the sciences and synthetic biology. Students will closely work with graduate students, faculty advisers, and professors to develop a research plan, to fundraise to support costs of team registration, participation, and research, to conduct research over the summer in on campus labs, and to work towards a human practices component of the project and competition. Among the ideals to be fostered by the UMD iGEM team are scholarship, dedication, communication, teamwork, curiosity, service to others through research and knowledge, and all the attributes desirable for a career in the sciences.

name: IMMERSE
description: IMMERSE (Immersive Media Makers Exploring Reality, Simulation, and Experiences) is a student-led organization at the University of Maryland that brings together students interested in immersive media, art, technology, design, and research. We strive to create a multidisciplinary community where students can explore immersive media through hands-on workshops, research panels, industry talks, design challenges, and collaborative projects. We also host social events, casual hangouts, and wellness-focused programs to help members build connections and feel supported within the community. Through our events, IMMERSE helps students develop creative and technical skills, discover academic and professional opportunities, and connect with others who share an interest in immersive experiences. Our goal is to foster an inclusive, welcoming space where students can learn, create, and grow at the intersection of art and technology. Our goal is to help students learn new skills, meet collaborators, discover career paths, and grow as creators and thinkers in areas like VR/AR, game design, installation art, VFX, HCI, creative coding, and interactive media. We aim to build an inclusive, multidisciplinary community where students can explore ideas, make meaningful connections, and create exciting work together.

name: Impact
description: Impact is established to create an environment where students are provided the opportunity to study the Bible in reference to the great commission given by Jesus in Matthew 28 as fulfilled in Acts 2. Impact understands and is committed to fulfilling its responsibilities of abiding by University of Maryland, College Park policies.

name: IMPACTnow
description: IMPACTnow is a student-led chapter at UMD, affiliated with the nonprofit IMPACTdmv, based out of Prince George's County, MD. Through workshops, community service, career & networking events, and community fundraisers we help all Terps build real life skills, confidence, and connections from freshman year to their first job. IMPACTnow works as long as you do!

name: Indian Student Association
description: The Indian Students Association is a non-profit, non-religious, non-politically affiliated organization of students whose purpose is to promote cultural awareness, diversity, and service to the community.

name: Indigenous at UMD
description: Indigenous at UMD is a coalition of Indigenous students, faculty/staff, and allies that seeks to unite and showcase Indigeneity via activism, education, scholarship, and attention to community issues on UMD’s campus. We endeavor to strengthen and advance the inter-tribal community on campus by uniting undergraduate and graduate Indigenous students as a community, both personally, culturally, and academically, throughout their journey.

name: Indonesian Student Association at the University of Maryland, College Park
description: This organization was founded out of the need to give Indonesian students a space to embrace the Indonesian community and identity. The purpose of this organization is to serve as a social and cultural hub for Indonesian students at the University of Maryland, College Park.

name: InfoSci FI
description: INFOSCI FI LINK TREE To become a member, please request membership on this TerpLink page. Once your request is approved, look for a "Welcome to InfoSci FI" email. Information Science is a major in technical areas including but not limited to data science, data curation, database administration, and cybersecurity ( Learn more about the UMD InfoSci Program ). InfoSciFI is dedicated to establishing the first Informational Science student organization at UMD to open up more opportunities for female-identifying students. These opportunities include developing a professional presence, providing volunteer experiences, and creating a positive environment for female-identifying students pursuing a career in technology.

name: Integrated Life Sciences Community Leadership Council
description: The Integrated Life Sciences Community Leadership Council (ILS CLC) is a group of students from the Integrated Life Sciences student body. Our goal is to support ILS students through the two-year honors program and beyond through academic, professional, and community engagement events and initiatives. CLC is dedicated to empowering and uniting the Integrated Life Sciences community through inclusive initiatives, fostering collaboration, and cultivating a sense of belonging through community-building events for all members. We are committed to improving the ILS experience by communicating the student voice to the ILS staff and actively engaging with the student body.

name: Intelligent Transportation Society and Institute of Transportation Engineers Student Chapter at the University of Maryland
description: The ITS-ITE UMD Student Chapter is a multidisciplinary student organization affiliated with the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE) and the Intelligent Transportation Society of America (ITS America). Our mission is to connect students with professionals in transportation engineering, planning, and technology. We host guest speakers, technical tours, networking events, and outreach activities to prepare students for leadership in the evolving field of transportation.

name: Intercollegiate Ethics Bowl
description: The Ethics Bowl Team meets twice per week to discuss issues ranging from Irish drunk driving policies to child labor laws. We compete in regional and national competitions where we have collaborative conversations with students from across the country!

name: Interdisciplinary Engineering Design Club
description: IEDC seeks to address the deficit of aesthetic design considerations in modern engineering education by fostering collaboration between disciplines and encouraging creativity, thoughtfulness, and beauty in everyday engineering practice and education.

name: Interfraternity Council Executive Board
description: As an intermediary between fraternities and the university, the Interfraternity Council at the University of Maryland is a representative governing body that supports and guides each member chapter toward reaching its greatest potential through promoting brotherhood, leadership, scholarship, service, facilitating interfraternal relations, and holding members and chapters to high moral standards by exemplifying a positive image to the campus, community, and beyond.

name: International Business Student Organization
description: Join our GroupMe to stay updated! https://groupme.com/join_group/96100109/8i19gsdB

name: International Economics and Finance Society
description: IEFS seeks to provide undergraduate students of all majors with knowledge and insight about international economics, finance, and trade, with a special focus on the global work environment. We help prepare undergraduate students for careers in these industries by relating theoretical knowledge to real-world issues and actively engaging with industry professionals.

name: International Friends Community
description: International Friends Community is a student-led organization at the University of Maryland, College Park, dedicated to supporting international students and individuals facing unique challenges. IFC goals are to offer mentorship, resources, networking opportunities, scholarships, and recreational events. The organization focuses on promoting social determinants of public health, particularly within the community context, to enhance the well-being of its members. By fostering a supportive environment that values diversity, inclusion, and equity, IFC encourages personal and academic growth, empowering individuals to succeed both at the university and beyond.

name: International Student Council
description: The International Student Council (ISC), formerly known as the International Student Advisory Board (ISAB) at the University of Maryland, established in Summer 2021 in collaboration with International Student and Scholar Services, is a dynamic force comprising 7 members representing diverse schools and departments. It is dedicated to enhancing international students' academic, professional, and social journey. It fulfills its mission by serving as a crucial link between the International student body and International Students and Scholar Services. Besides this, its other important commitments include identifying and addressing issues and challenges international students face and effectively communicating valuable resources to the international student community at UMD. Aligning with the university's policy to create an environment that embraces and celebrates the richness of our diverse student body, ISAB is dedicated to fostering a welcoming and inclusive atmosphere for all international students.

name: InterVarsity Graduate Christian Fellowship
description: InterVarsity Graduate Christian Fellowship is a community focused on welcoming graduate students from all different walks of life; introducing, renewing and challenging their faith; and equipping them to be sent back out as witnesses of God's Kingdom. We believe in the fullness of the Gospel of Jesus Christ and it's power to restore as well as inspire us in our daily lives. With this in mind, we pursue relationships with those around us and with those in unreached communities on and off campus. Through building relationships both inside and outside of our fellowship, we aim to learn and grow in Christ with one another by seeing how God is working in the lives, experiences, cultures, ethnicities, and identities of us all. All are welcome, so come check us out!

name: Introverts Club
description: We are an organization dedicated to creating a comfortable and welcoming space for students who identify as introverts. We know that building connections is a big part of the university experience, but it can be challenging for introverted students in a world that often values extroversion. Our club provides opportunities to meet like-minded individuals, be your authentic self, and enjoy a calm, stress-free environment. Beyond social connection, we challenge stereotypes about introverts, support each other in developing new skills, and celebrate the unique strengths we bring as introverts.

name: Investing Club
description: A place for UMD students to explore investing, discuss current news, share ideas and resources, and take part in club and external investing competitions.

name: Iranian Graduate Student Foundation (IGSF)
description: IGSF is a non-profitable, non-religious, non-political organization, established for the expressed purpose of developing leadership skills as well as an awareness of social responsibilities to encourage students to participate in public affairs. Also, IGSF tends to praise and promote Iranian traditions and culture and make people familiar with these traditions.

name: IRANIAN STUDENTS' FOUNDATION
description: Welcome to the Iranian Students' Foundation! Our mission is to unite students who are interested in Iranian culture, build a stronger presence on the greater UMD campus, and maintain a bond with the neighboring Iranian-American communities. We are a social club focused on bringing together Iranian-American students and creating an atmosphere of community, positivity, and friendship.

name: Islamic Center of North America Relief at The University of Maryland
description: The purpose of the organization is to be established for the purpose of inspiring and empowering students to support local and international communities through hands-on relief work, skill-building workshops, and educational campaigns guided by faith-inspired values of compassion and service. The organization also aims at building and maintaining partnerships, representing the organization, and coordinating collaborative efforts to build a strong community on campus and raise awareness about different cultures to encourage and advocate for diversity and inclusiveness.

name: J Street UMD
description: Pro-Israel, pro-Palestine, pro-peace students advocating for an end to the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories.

name: Jackie's Kitchen
description: We are a service organization dedicated to recovering food from UMD's campus Hillel that would otherwise be wasted and distributing the recovered food to local families struggling with food insecurity.

name: Jammin' at Maryland
description: This club is a chill place to create music with fellow UMD musicians. We don’t use sheet music! We usually do covers of songs but sometimes we do our own thing and create something new. You don’t need to be a musical expert to enjoy the jam sessions. All you need to do is bring yourself, your instrument/voice, and be ready to have some fun! Our members may optionally reserve time on the Baltimore Room Stage during our regular meetings to rehearse or improvise a performance of their choosing. Be sure to join our Discord by clicking the globe below! Almost all meeting and event notifications are done via our discord, so it is necessary in order to access the basic how-to's to navigate the club and to be up to date. Discord: https://discord.gg/MNDjCgXuR Request Sheet: JAM Weekly Request Sheet

name: Japanese American Student Association
description: We work to create an environment in which we can build a community, whether it be with Japanese/Japanese-American students, or those who are interested in some aspect of Japanese culture, language, or arts! Our events will vary year by year; follow us on Instagram, and/or Discord to start getting involved! Instagram; @umcpjasa Link to Discord!

name: Jewish Athletics Group
description: Jewish Athletics Group is established for the expressed purpose of providing major athletic and athletic-related events to the University of Maryland Jewish community, including the National Hillel Basketball Tournament and other competitive athletic events.

name: Jewish Student Union
description: The Jewish Student Union provides social and cultural programming for the University of Maryland Community by offering events to students of all backgrounds. We provide large and small scale programs geared towards creating and sustaining a Jewish network and community on campus.

name: Journaling Club
description: Students who share a passion for journaling or want to explore a new hobby of journaling can gather in one space to create journal spreads or share their spreads and ideas. This will help foster a relieving environment an encourages creativity.

name: Journey Christian Fellowship
description: This student group shall be conducted as a community service group with the goal of serving high schools in Maryland by providing resources to help prepare students for college.

name: Juggling Club
description: The Juggling Club serves as a forum for teaching, learning, and performing juggling and other related arts of object manipulation. Once a year, we also hold a convention that draws jugglers from surrounding states.

name: Jump Rope Club at University of Maryland
description: This organization is here to promote the sport of jump rope along with growth in a healthy lifestyle. We will participate in fitness related activities involving jump rope. While building a community among peers.

name: Justice for Fraud Victims
description: A nonprofit organization affiliated with the University of Maryland Our goal is to provide free assistance to victims of financial fraud. Fraud can be confusing, costly, and time-consuming. We are here to help.

name: Kairos Christian Fellowship
description: Kairos is a Christian student group on the UMD campus that meets weekly to study the Bible and find out God’s perspective for our lives. Kairos is the Greek word for "an opportune time" and this is exactly what we believe college to be... an opportune time for you to make lifelong friendships and memories, and delve into life’s bigger questions. At Kairos, we provide a comfortable environment where these types of questions can be discussed and answered. More than that, we strive to “do life” together whether it’s studying late into the night for an exam, going on fun getaways, service opportunities, eating some good food, or just hanging out! So whether you’re a Christian looking for discipleship or someone seeking to find out more about Christianity, come join us as we take advantage of this “opportune time”!

name: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity Incorporated
description: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. is a collegiate Greek-letter fraternity. Founded on January 5, 1911 at Indiana University Bloomington, the organization has never limited membership based on color, creed, or national origin. Our motto is honorable achievement in every field of human endeavor and one of the main focused actions is training for leadership.

name: Kappa Alpha Theta
description: Yesterday, today, and tomorrow, Kappa Alpha Theta exists to nurture each member throughout her college and alumnae experience and to offer a lifelong opportunity for social, intellectual and moral growth as she meets the higher and broader demands of mature life.

name: Kappa Delta Pi
description: Kappa Delta Pi is an international educational honor society for future professionals in the field of education. We inspire professionals to thrive and build a community to create lifelong opportunities and provide equitable education for all.

name: Kappa Delta Sorority
description: Kappa Delta Sorority aims to promote true friendship among the college students of our country by inculcating academics, philanthropy, and social activities in their lives. For more information please visit our website at umd.kappadelta.org.

name: Kappa Kappa Psi Fraternity Gamma Xi
description: Kappa Kappa Psi is a co-educational fraternal organization that advances college and university bands for the benefit of its members and society through dedicated service and support to bands, encouragement of musical growth, lifelong educational experiences, leadership opportunities, and recognition.

name: Kappa Lambda Xi Multicultural Sorority, Inc.
description: The dedicated ladies of the Alpha Chapter of Kappa Lambda Xi Sorority are intent upon their mission of Unity in Diversity and Breaking Down Barriers to rid preexisting notions of prejudice, discrimination and false pride on campus and in the surrounding community through the strong bonds of sisterhood. The young women are expected to instill in their hearts the meaning of sisterhood, and to grow and bloom and become sisters in mind and spirit, sisters with grace and integrity, and sisters who become the leaders of tomorrow.

name: Kappa Omega Alpha Policy Professional Fraternity Gamma Chapter
description: The purpose of this Fraternity shall be to acknowledge students in pursuit of their interests in the field of public policy on both a social and professional scale; to uphold the strength of fraternalism; to strengthen the ideals of Kappa Omega Alpha Co-ed Fraternity; to participate actively in the community and campus; and to ensure that each member develops into leaders within their field of policy interest.

name: Kappa Phi Lambda Sorority, Inc.
description: We, the sisters of Kappa Phi Lambda Sorority, Incorporated, strive to strengthen sisterhood amongst women by providing service and promoting cultural diversity to our members and our community, thus securing the bond of kinship for posterity. Kappa Phi Lambda exists to further educate individuals about Pan-Asian culture, while keeping our own identities. We aim for academic excellence, keeping in mind the importance of education and learning as the key to strength, awareness, and fulfillment.

name: Kappa Sigma Fraternity
description: Founded in 1869 at the University of Virginia, Kappa Sigma is one of the largest and most prestigious collegiate fraternities in North America. The fraternity is rooted in the core values of fellowship, leadership, scholarship, and service. With over 200 active chapters and colonies across the United States and Canada, Kappa Sigma promotes the personal development of its members through brotherhood, academic excellence, philanthropic involvement, and leadership opportunities. Kappa Sigma’s mission is to complement and enhance the educational experience of college men by offering a values-based fraternity experience. The fraternity emphasizes a strong commitment to the Four Pillars: to strive for excellence in scholarship, build lasting bonds of brotherhood, cultivate leadership abilities, and give back through service to the community. Through initiatives such as the Kappa Sigma Endowment Fund and A Greater Cause program, members are empowered to achieve their potential and positively impact their campuses and communities.

name: Kappa Theta Pi
description: Kappa Theta Pi is a co-ed professional technology fraternity at the University of Maryland. KTP is open to all students with an interest in technology, regardless of major. Students can rush and pledge each fall and spring semester to become a brother.

name: Kedma
description: We are the Orthodox Community at UMD! Get involved through Torah learning, social events, Chessed (acts of kindness) opportunities, Shabbat meals, and so much more!

name: Kendo Club at the University of Maryland
description: We are the Kendo Club at UMD! Practice the ancient Japanese sword martial art and compete at the collegiate level! Most importantly, our club aims to preserve the traditions of the art and help bring enriching and character-building practice to UMD.

name: Kesem at University of Maryland
description: Kesem is a nationwide community, driven by passionate college student leaders, that supports children through and beyond their parent's cancer. A program of Kesem, Camp Kesem operates free summer camps and year round support for children who have been touched by a parent's cancer. Watch our CKUMD camp 2019 videos HERE and HERE !

name: Kharis Campus Ministry
description: To know God and make Him known at the University of Maryland, done through: Large Groups with music and a message, Focus Families for Bible studies, Small Groups for fellowship, Prayer Meetings to seek and depend on God, Outreach learning to love others and to share the Gospel, Special events to spend time with each person made in God’s image. Our goal is to build a Christ-centered community and be a light on our campus.

name: Kick for a cause
description: Kick for a Cause is a heartwarming community initiative at the University of Maryland. We transform a shared love for soccer into a powerful mission of hope, uniting people through play to champion critical health causes, including leukemia. With every goal, we support vital medical research and the brave individuals facing these challenges.

name: Kidney Disease Screening and Awareness Program at The University of Maryland, College Park
description: As defined by the parent organization, the goals of the KDSAP’s community outreach are (1) to identify risk factors of kidney disease, which will lead to early referrals, and (2) to prevent the development of kidney disease. Therefore, KDSAP screenings are not only intended to treat but also to educate the community and raise the awareness of kidney disease. A large part of our organization is our unwavering commitment to serve our community with compassion and humility.

name: Kids Helping Kids
description: Through a partnership with Johns Hopkins Pediatric Oncology, Kids Helping Kids raises awareness and funds for pediatric oncology research. By hosting fundraising events, this service organization will work towards educating others, encouraging a selfless environment, and saving lives.

name: Kinesiology Student Organization
description: The Kinesiology Student Organization (KSO) at the University of Maryland is dedicated to fostering academic, professional, and social growth among Kinesiology students. Our mission is to provide members with valuable tools and opportunities to succeed in their studies, prepare for their careers, and build a strong, supportive community. KSO offers a platform for students to network with peers, faculty, and professionals, engage in community service, and access expert resources. Through these initiatives, we aim to enhance the undergraduate and postgraduate experience while strengthening the UMD Kinesiology community.

name: KOINONIA
description: KOINONIA is a Christian student organization that aims to preach the gospel and encourage Christian fellowship among students through praise, Bible study, and group activities. To learn more about us, check out our website: https://www.washingtonubf.org/college

name: KOL SASSON JEWISH A CAPPELLA SINGERS
description: Founded in 1997 as the University of Maryland’s premier Jewish a cappella group, Kol Sasson has been serving the national Jewish community with song for over twenty years. Comprised of students from all backgrounds, studies, and cities around the country, the members of Kol Sasson come together to perform repertoire ranging from English and Israeli pop to traditional Jewish melodies, and more. Check out kolsasson.com for more information!

name: Korean Graduate Student Association
description: The Korean Graduate Student Association has been established to increase close cooperation and unity among the members. KGSA provides opportunities of the better academic life and the better understanding of Korean culture to the students and the community.

name: Korean Pop Dance Club
description: "Korean Pop Dance Club" (otherwise known as Ganji) was established for the expressed purpose of exploring Korean Culture and learning K-Pop choreography in a relaxed, non-judgmental environment. We hold workshops that are open to anyone in the UMCP community and no prior dance experience is required! We also perform at various events across campus like TASA's Night Market, JASA's Taste of Japan, and more! Follow us on social media to keep updated with workshops, general body meetings, and performances (Instagram/TikTok: @ganjiumd, Discord:https://discord.gg/pZrQwMc2Ux)! Hope to see you there!

name: Korean Student Association
description: To promote Korean culture and provide a safe community for expanding and expressing interest in Korean culture while meeting new people and making new friends.

name: Kreativity Diversity Troupe
description: Kreativity Diversity Troupe is a performing arts group on campus dedicated to uplifting the array of voices that exist in the UMD student body! We put on an end of semester showcase of scenes every semester with works of all formats: dances, skits, vignettes to larger works, film, digital art, visual art, music, spoken word and the totally unique things that spring from collaboration! make sure to follow us on social media and don't hesitate to audition any semester, no matter what year you are.

name: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Inc. - Phi Chapter
description: Phi Chapter was founded on December 10th, 1995 by 9 men of different backgrounds, but with the same goal of fulfilling the needs of our community. Phi Chapter has done an extensive job on establishing a presence for Latinos at the University of Maryland through various community service initiatives and educational programming such as our annual Latino/a Bienvenida welcome orientation, and annual Toy Drives. Considering that we are undergraduate students, we continue to think of and expand on new programs to educate the University and Latino community. We hope that your visit here is both informative and helpful.

name: La Voz Latina
description: La Voz Latina is an independent student-run newspaper dedicated to covering both the Latino community on the University of Maryland, College Park campus and broader issues that affect Latinos nationwide. We are a Latino-interest, but not Latino exclusive organization. That means our workers do not have to be of Latino descent and/or know Spanish to work for us – in fact, anyone can work for us. Staff Writers will be tasked to write various kinds of stories (news, opinion, entertainment, culture, and sports) every week. Alongside our writers are our Section Editors and Copy Editors. Last but not least, our paper wouldn't be complete without the help from other talented students interested in website design, social media, art, and business operations. That said, we invite all interested students to reach out about available positions, meetings, and upcoming publications.

name: LACS Graduate Collective
description: We are a collective of graduate student-workers from Latin America and the Caribbean. We are Latinx. We are Latin Americanist and Caribbeanist scholars with divergent paths, personal trajectories, educational backgrounds, and research interests. Our association comprises different activities throughout the academic year. First, we offer a writing group with the goal of supporting and providing feedback on scholarly research about Latin America including academic papers, presentations, public writing. Second, graduates form a conference committee that organizes and leads LASC's annual student conference. Third, group members provide a social network that meets on and off-campus for different events. Members of the collective can part of one or more of these subsets. The LASC graduate community grew out of the 2015 Annual Conference “Hybridity: Examining Processes of Circulation, Collaboration, and Conflict.” Nine students from across campus met to discuss the theme, organize the panels, and propose and select keynote speakers. After the conference in summer 2016 we founded the LASC Writing Group. For three years we have been meeting regularly to 1) create a space for discussion and intellectual exchange where students can share and construct knowledge that reaches across disciplines and experiences, 2) to explore interdisciplinary approaches in our research, 3) to facilitate a more holistic approach to professional development by engaging students with topics, research, questions, theories, and methodologies that are outside our fields, and 4) to generate a collaborative network among graduate students to share materials, sources, scholarship, and contacts that contribute to our research and experiences.

name: Lambda Chi Alpha
description: A fraternity dedicated to the cultivation of good men through scholarship, leadership, community service, and brotherly love.

name: Lambda Pi Delta at The University of Maryland
description: Lambda Pi Delta serves as a dedicated platform for students passionate about French language and literature, aiming to bolster their academic pursuits through dynamic projects and leadership initiatives. Our mission is to empower students to take the lead in shaping their French education, offering a space where they can engage in meaningful activities and impactful projects that complement their studies.

name: Lambda Theta Alpha Latin Sorority, Inc. -Upsilon Chapter
description: Lambda Theta Alpha was recognized at Kean University in 1975 as the First Latina Sorority founded in the United States. This organization was the first to recognize the need for a support system, thus creating one. It allowed the independent Latina woman of a new era to have a sense of belonging and with that, achieve her highest potential. It would define a new role for the Latina woman, one with education, goals and vision in hopes of great success. Now, several decades later, we have seen the outcome of such an organization. Lambda Theta Alpha has contributed to the advancement of all people by helping to produce educated women of many races, ethnicities, and creeds. These women are political leaders, doctors, lawyers, teachers, accountants, etc. LTA has also paved the way for many other Latina organizations, which would later pursue the empowering movement that we set the trend for. From 1975 to date, Lambda Theta Alpha has upheld its purpose and mission, each day realizing the Founder's dream - that it may serve as a quintessential trailblazer for all women.

name: Latino Pre-Law Society
description: The Latino Pre-Law Society is dedicated to cultivating a dynamic community that empowers students that are not adequately represented in the profession of Law, to aspire/ to pursue careers in law. Our mission is to foster academic excellence, professional development, and a strong sense of identity within the legal field. We intend to provide a space and create awareness for students interested in pursuing a career in law.

name: Latino Student Union
description: The Latin Student Union (LSU) at the University of Maryland is a vibrant and dynamic organization that provides a welcoming and inclusive space for the Latine community on campus. As a cultural, educational, political, and social outlet, we strive to celebrate and promote Latinx culture, traditions, and experiences not just for the Latine community but for anyone who is interested in appreciating our culture with us! Our organization serves as a resource for Latinx students, offering support, guidance, and mentorship to help them thrive academically and personally. We host a variety of events, including cultural celebrations, educational workshops, political discussions, and social gatherings, to engage and connect our members! Within LSU, we believe in creating a sense of belonging and camaraderie within the Latine community at the University of Maryland. Our goal is to foster lasting friendships, build a strong support network, and create a familia where all students feel welcomed, valued, and empowered to succeed because si se puede! Join us at LSU and be a part of a community that celebrates diversity, embraces inclusivity, and promotes unity among Latinx students at the University of Maryland. Come find your home away from home and become a part of our familia!

name: Latinos in Computing
description: A student-led club building community for Latino students in tech and computing at UMD. We offer guest speakers, career resources, project tracks, and workshops, all are welcome regardless of major or experience.

name: Latinx Architects United
description: A group of latinx architecture students. Not exclusive to only latinx students. We strive to promote and endorse higher education in latinx culture through the architecture pathway.

name: Latinx Pre-Health Society
description: The purpose of the Latinx Pre-Health Society is to prepare students with a Latinx background and other backgrounds for a career in a healthcare profession. The organization focuses on helping students not only academically but professionally as well.

name: Latter-day Saints Student Association
description: The University of Maryland chapter of the Latter-day Saint Student Association (LDSSA) serves as a connection between UMD students and the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. We promote a welcoming environment where students are supported and respected as they strive to achieve their social, academic, and spiritual goals. We host events that promote service, community, and faith. All are welcome! LDSSA was established under the direction of the Seminaries and Institutes of Religion of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

name: Lean On Me College Park
description: Lean On Me College Park aims to provide UMD students with non-crisis, peer-to-peer text-based emotional support anytime, anywhere. We also hope to promote mental health advocacy and awareness on campus through partnerships and events. If you are interested in joining or would like to know more, check out our Instagram @lom_collegepark or visit our website !

name: Leatherbacks Combat Robotics
description: UMD's combat robotics club. We design, build, and fight our own robots, just like the BattleBots TV show. Our bots range from 1-30lbs. Our discord link is below. You can also find us on the Discord UMD hub. https://discord.gg/TJsdgHt4bf

name: LeBron James Club at the University of Maryland
description: Link to instagram: https://www.instagram.com/umd_lebronclub?igsh=MWMxOWNyd2s3aDJqdA%3D%3D&utm_source=qr Link to groupme: https://groupme.com/join_group/99195879/5OhMzoZg

name: Legally Speaking
description: A safe space where everyone can share their thoughts on the legal world + a platform to publish legal writing. We discuss legal topics such as court cases, laws we agree/disagree with, controversial issues, and anything related to the legal system.

name: Let's Dance Club
description: Club meetings will be split between dancing through the video game Just Dance (with free, online platforms like Just Dance Now and/or YouTube), and working on the yearly video project. The video project will culminate in a choreographed "Just Dance" video posted on the club YouTube channel. This video will essentially be a dance, choreographed by members, to a song selected by members. There will also be a video editing team for students to edit the background and add effects, and member faces will all be edited out for privacy reasons. The goal of this club is to foster a fun and supportive atmosphere, where students can dance in an inclusive environment, and to offer a creative outlet for those who wish to participate in the video project. Meetings will be structured so that the first half hour consists of dancing, and the second half hour consists of project work. This way, those who wish to join for whichever, or both, component(s) may do so.

name: Little STEMs
description: Little Stems exists to make STEM topics more approachable to younger students and to foster excitement, curiosity, and exploration through volunteer-led events at elementary schools, middle schools, community centers, and youth programs on campus.

name: Love For Our Elders at the University of Maryland
description: We are the University of Maryland chapter of Love For Our Elders, a nonprofit dedicated to combating social isolation among older adults. Through handwritten letters, intergenerational connections, and community outreach, we bring UMD students together to brighten the lives of seniors and spread kindness across our community.

name: LSAMP STEM
description: The LSAMP STEM Community is a professional STEM student organization committed to providing a community and resources for students in STEM to thrive personally and professionally. Our theme is “Bridging the gap between STEM students and career opportunities”. We look forward to collaborating with companies and sponsors to host impactful workshops that develop members into strong, confident candidates for internships, research, and full-time roles.

name: Make-A-Wish at the University of Maryland
description: We are working with the Make-A-Wish Mid-Atlantic chapter to bring this club to life. We plan to host events in partnership with Make-A-Wish to interact with the community and beyond.

name: Makerspace For All Club
description: The Makerspace For All Club promotes and supports access for Makerspace technologies and trainings for all undergraduate students, regardless of financial ability, at the University of Maryland, College Park.

name: Mario Kart Club
description: Anyone is free to join & all skill levels are welcome! We run weekly tournaments every Friday @ 5 pm in Stamp! We also have a competitive team & compete in multiple collegiate leagues! Discord Server: https://discord.gg/ZWSenqBevm

name: Martial Arts Club
description: The Martial Arts Club has been established for the purpose of integrating as many styles to gain a wider perspective on the martial arts collective; and to facilitate the interactions of martial artists from different backgrounds and incorporate them effectively. The club also allows members to experience self defense and aerobic exercises. Find our socials and communication platforms on our Linktree! https://linktr.ee/ umdmartialarts?fbclid= PAZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAAab2flELQdw5 zvXcBXFvtysHXAH_SpQ- aUZXnje79o5FKakYzAOYzc6AW4Y_ aem_AOZjgBtCTmbyCT6ZifagyA Join our "team" on IMLeagues (Required by RecWell): https://www.imleagues.com/spa/team/89d78cce167e446391bd306f8ea5c587/home (You must complete the required forms and concussion quiz to participate during practice)

name: Maryland Association of Black Journalists
description: MABJ is a pre-professional organization for students working toward degrees in journalism at the University of Maryland. We work together under the auspice of the National Association of Black Journalists in educating its members with respect to the journalism field. We also assist with the pursuit of scholarships, internships and networking opportunities.

name: Maryland Badminton
description: We're the Badminton Club at UMD. We're all super friendly, welcoming to players of all levels, and hope you'll give us a shot. We provide birdies and rackets, so all you have to do is come to practice and we'll set you up with everything you need. Sign up on imleagues to join us. We don't post much on TerpLink; we use Discord and Facebook that tells you how to join. Discord: https://discord.gg/w7XwATJueN Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/umdclubbadminton

name: Maryland Beit Midrash
description: Maryland Beit Midrash is a student-run organization, focusing on making Judaic textual learning at the University of Maryland, College Park more abundant, accessible, and alive.

name: Maryland Bhangra
description: We are the University of Maryland's premiere co-ed bhangra team! Established in 2010, Maryland Bhangra strives to bring an entertaining performance while maintaining the traditional and folk roots from Punjab. Go Terps!

name: Maryland Bollywood
description: Maryland Bollywood is a student organization dedicated to celebrating all aspects of Bollywood, such as dance, film, music, and community. Our goal is to create an inclusive space for students to explore South Asian culture and connect with others. Through events like karaoke nights, film discussions, dance workshops, and fundraisers, we aim to share Bollywood culture’s storytelling, rhythm, and celebration with our campus community.

name: Maryland Club Baseball
description: Maryland is one of a handful of schools that have both a D1 and D2 team in the NCBA. Both teams compete against other schools in the Mid Atlantic and wish to return to the National World Series.

name: Maryland Club Cheer
description: Univeristy of Maryland Club Cheerleading is an independent non-profit organization dedicated to promoting the sport of cheerleading.

name: Maryland Club Climbing
description: UMD Club Climbing is a student-led organization that welcomes climbers of all skill levels, from complete beginners to more experienced athletes. We aim to create a supportive and encouraging community where members can learn, improve, and enjoy climbing together. The club offers opportunities to climb both at commercial climbing gyms in the area and outdoors at nearby crags, giving members a variety of experiences throughout the year. In addition to climbing opportunities, the club hosts competitions and social events that help members build skills, connect with others, and become part of the climbing community. The club also owns gear that members can use free of charge during practices, making it easy for anyone to get involved. We offer two types of practices. Club meetings are primarily social and take place on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 8:00 p.m. to 9:45 p.m., when the outdoor wall is open (10:00 pm to 11:45 pm when it is closed). Development team practices are more focused on skill-building and take place on Mondays and Wednesdays from 10:00 p.m. to 11:45 p.m. Whether you are trying climbing for the first time or looking to grow as a climber, our club is a great place to learn, challenge yourself, and meet others who share your interest.

name: Maryland Club Flag Football
description: Maryland Club Flag Football is open to all undergraduate students of the University of Maryland and our goal is to compete in intercollegiate tournaments, socialize, and have fun playing the sport we all love.

name: Maryland Club Golf
description: Maryland Club Golf is established for the expressed purpose of providing students leadership opportunities and instilling core values such as honesty, responsibility and integrity. Those who are passionate about the sport will enjoy our competitive environment in the intercollegiate club while those who are new to the game will have the opportunity to learn, develop and experience all aspects of the game.

name: Maryland Club Gymnastics Team
description: The Maryland Club Gymnastics Team is established for the expressed purpose of extending the opportunity of competitive gymnastics to all who are interested and to provide a positive gymnastics experience for all participants.

name: Maryland Club Roller Hockey
description: Our mission is to provide a fun, welcoming, and affordable way for students to get involved in hockey while building a strong community through the sport. We offer local competition through the DC Hockey League (DCHL), giving members the opportunity to play regularly without the higher costs often associated with traditional hockey. Through our participation in the National Collegiate Roller Hockey Association (NCRHA), we also hope to compete in weekend tournaments along the East Coast, including events in Philadelphia, Rhode Island, and New York. These NCRHA opportunities allow our team to represent the University of Maryland, compete against other collegiate programs, strengthen team connections, and become part of a larger collegiate roller hockey community.

name: Maryland Club Roundnet
description: UMD Spikeball Hype Video

name: Maryland Club Running
description: Maryland Club Running’s mission is to promote participation/competition within the National Intercollegiate Running Club Association (NIRCA), and National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division 1 and Division 3 cross country and track meets for the general body of students at the University of Maryland, College Park wishing to race in a competitive environment. We aim to foster an inclusive environment to ensure all levels of ability may participate within the club both for practice and competition.

name: Maryland Club Soccer
description: We are a competitive, student-run club that loves to play great-quality soccer. Any Maryland student is welcome to join any of our practices.
